# weblate_category (Resource)

Manages a Weblate Category, a folder inside a Project that groups Components. Categories can nest up to three levels deep.

Changing `name` or `slug` renames the Category in place, and changing `category` moves it in place. Weblate cannot move a Category to another Project, so changing `project` to another Project fails on apply. When `project` changes because the Project was renamed, only the state changes. Delete waits until Weblate has removed the Category in the background.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "weblate_category" "guides" {
  project = weblate_project.docs.slug
  name    = "Guides"
  slug    = "guides"
}

resource "weblate_category" "api" {
  project  = weblate_project.docs.slug
  category = weblate_category.guides.id
  name     = "API reference"
  slug     = "api"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the Category. Unique among the Categories with the same parent.
- `project` (String) Slug of the Project that holds the Category.
- `slug` (String) Slug of the Category, as in its URL. Unique among the Categories with the same parent.

### Optional

- `category` (String) `id` of the parent Category, which is its slug path and must start with `project`. Without it, the Category is at the root of the Project.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The slug path of the Category: the Project slug and the slugs of all Categories down to this one, joined by `/`, such as `docs/guides`.
- `weblate_id` (Number) Numeric ID that Weblate gave the Category. It stays the same when the Category is renamed or moved.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `delete` (String) How long to wait for Weblate to delete the Category in the background, such as `30m`. Defaults to `20m`. When the time is up, the deletion goes on in Weblate.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the slug path of the Category, such as docs/guides/api.
terraform import weblate_category.api docs/guides/api
```
